title: capacity-flexibility-runway-scenario-matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet is a compact scenario matrix that connects short-term demand forecasts to recommended reserved capacity, burst policies, and expected GPU-hour spend. It is explicit about key assumptions (model kernels, tokens/hr per GPU, cache hit rate, util) and includes sensitivity axes for cache hit rate and batching. Use this to feed the Optimize cost model and to create the Reserved vs Burst ask for finance and sales ops.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline (P50) steady growth: 12% month-over-month for next 6 months.
- P90 tail/load spikes increase required GPU-hours by ~2.1x relative to baseline when cache hit rate stays low (5% hit).
- Recommended initial reserved commit: 60% of baseline peak-month required GPUs with a 20% headroom buffer; rest handled via burst/autoscale.
- Optimization levers with most impact: caching (KV/prefix) and lowering tokens/req via summary prompts. Quantization gives ~25-40% GPU token throughput improvement for compatible variants.

Assumptions and constants (edit these cells):
- Forecast granularity: monthly
- Time horizon: 6 months (Jan - Jun 2025)
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for interactive routes, batch can be higher
- Effective GPU throughput (tokens/hr) by model family (unquantized, util=0.7):
  - Llama-2-13B: 900M tokens/hr
  - Mistral-70B: 1.6B tokens/hr (quantization / kernel dependent)
  - Redwood-optimized-medium: 1.2B tokens/hr
- Tokenization and request averages are best-effort measured from sample traces (Dec 2024)
- Cost per GPU hour (on Dedicated pool list): $2.85 / GPU-hr (baseline for on-demand internal accounting)
- Quantization multiplier (tokens/hr improvement): 1.35 (conservative)
- KV/prefix cache hit rates: baseline 15%, optimistic 45%
- Autoscaler min pods = reserved GPUs, burst limit = reserved * 3 (configurable)

Primary table (columns and formula notes) - example rows for three scenarios:
Columns: Month | Scenario | Requests/day | Avg tokens/req | Tokens/day | Model | Eff tokens/hr/GPU | Utilization | GPU-hours/day | GPUs required (24h farm) | Reserved GPUs recommended | Burst capacity suggested | Daily infra $ | Notes
Formulas (text):
- Tokens/day = Requests/day * Avg tokens/req
- GPU-hours/day = Tokens/day / Eff tokens/hr/GPU / Utilization
- GPUs required (24h farm) = ceil(GPU-hours/day / 24)
- Reserved GPUs recommended = floor(GPUs required * reserved_commit_pct) (round up to nearest allowed SKU)
- Daily infra $ = GPU-hours/day * cost_per_gpu_hr

Example rows: (baseline throughput values shown)
1) 2025-03 | Baseline (P50) | 1,400,000 req/day | 320 tokens | 448,000,000 tokens/day | Redwood-optimized-medium | 1.2B tokens/hr | 0.72 util | 0.52 GPU-hrs/day | 1 GPU | reserved 1 GPU | burst up to 3 GPUs | $1.48/day | small interactive workload, high multi-tenancy
2) 2025-03 | Growth spike (P90 short) | 2,800,000 req/day | 420 tokens | 1,176,000,000 tokens/day | Llama-2-13B | 900M tokens/hr | 0.65 util | 2.01 GPU-hrs/day | 1 GPU | reserved 1 GPU | burst up to 3 GPUs | $5.73/day | multi-route traffic spike, latency-sensitive
3) 2025-04 | Optimized caching + quant | 2,400,000 req/day | 320 tokens | 768,000,000 tokens/day | Llama-2-13B (quant) | 1.215B tokens/hr (1.35x) | 0.72 util | 0.88 GPU-hrs/day | 1 GPU | reserved 1 GPU | burst up to 3 GPUs | $2.51/day | cache hit 40% reduces tokens pushed to GPU

Sensitivity matrix (text table):
Axes: cache hit rate (5%, 15%, 30%, 50%) vs batching/avg latency (no-batch p95 200ms, small-batch +20ms, large-batch +60ms).
- Observed delta in GPU-hrs/day for a fixed request volume (2M req/day, 300 tokens/req):
  - 5% hit -> baseline GPU-hrs/day = 1.85
  - 15% hit -> GPU-hrs/day = 1.57 (-15%)
  - 30% hit -> GPU-hrs/day = 1.30 (-30%)
  - 50% hit -> GPU-hrs/day = 0.92 (-50%)
- Batching improves tokens/hr effective by 1.1x (small-batch) to 1.45x (large-batch) but increases tail latency. Use for non-interactive workloads.

Runway calc (6 month):
- Input a monthly requests/day forecast vector (example): [1.2M, 1.35M, 1.5M, 1.68M, 1.88M, 2.10M]
- Convert to tokens/day using per-route avg tokens; aggregate by model family 
- Estimate GPU-hours/month and $/month using cost_per_gpu_hr and utilization schedule (weekday peaks, off-peak lower util)
- Plot cumulative committed spend vs on-demand spend to find break-even month for reserved commits.

Break-even heuristics (rules of thumb):
- If predicted sustained GPU-hours/month per SKU > 0.7 * (reserved_gpus * 24 * 30), reserved capacity often favored (depending on contract discounts).
- Prefer reserved commits for stable, predictable route traffic (>= 60% of total tokens) and keep <40% for burst (unpredictable spikes).

Optimization recommendations (short list):
1) Short-term (0-3 months): increase cache TTLs on prefixes and enable light quant for non-sensitive routes; reserve 50-60% of baseline peak GPUs.
2) Medium-term (3-9 months): instrument per-route token counts and build per-customer headroom curves; negotiate reserved commit discounts for >6-month commitment.
3) Architecture: route high-latency tolerant workloads to batched endpoints with larger batch sizes and quantized model variants.
4) Autoscaler config: set min to reserved, max to reserved*3 for now; add predictive ramp-up for expected daily peak windows.
5) Cost-savings experiments to run (A/B): 1) quantized vs full model on 10% of traffic; 2) aggressive KV cache on FAQs + onboarding flows (measure hit rate uplift).

Open questions / decision points (todo):
- Confirm contract discount curves for 6m and 12m reserved commits with finance (linked JIRA OPT-412).
- Agree on acceptable p95 tail increase for batched endpoints (trade-off between cost and UX).
- Decide on the set of models approved for quantized serving in Dedicated pools.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus Li: run a 2-week quant A/B on the onboarding route and report tokens/hr delta (due 2025-02-28).
- Owain Patel: instrument the per-route token telemetry (patch infra-exporter) and drop sample traces into /datasets/optimize/requests-samples (due 2025-02-20).
- Anika Desai: prepare reserved vs burst ask for sales/finance with two commitment tiers (due 2025-03-05).

Notes on document usage:
- This doc is a working sheet — numbers are provisional. Please copy to a stable workbook before finalizing any commitments.
- When updating: change the constants block and then regenerate the primary table rows; keep a copy of old forecasts for audit.

Appendix - quick sample calculation (verbatim):
Given: 2M req/day, avg 300 tokens/req -> 600M tokens/day. Using Llama-2-13B unquantized (900M tokens/hr) at util=0.7 -> tokens/hr effective = 630M tokens/hr. GPU-hours/day = 600M / 630M = 0.95 GPU-hrs/day -> GPUs required = ceil(0.95 / 24) = 1 GPU. Daily infra $ = 0.95 * $2.85 = $2.71/day.

Change log (high level):
- 2025-01-09 initial draft (Anika)
- 2025-01-22 added sensitivity matrix (Owain)
- 2025-02-15 updated assumptions and action items (Marcus)

End of sheet.
